sample.justification: Bingley's arrival sets a clear marriage-market question, but the scene is largely comic dialogue establishing character rather than driving events.
Jane and Elizabeth's post-ball talk and Bingley/Darcy background are reflective exposition with little forward push.
Netherfield dinner deepens Darcy-Elizabeth friction and Bingley's sisters' snobbery, advancing relationships steadily but without urgency.

cases.summary: Inquiry returned 17 finding(s) over 61 scenes; verdict and refs passed the production result builder.

sample.summary: The story moves smoothly because the early Hertfordshire chapters load nearly every later payoff in advance. The entail, the militia's timetable, Bingley's pliability, Darcy's unforgiving temper and Wickham's checkable claims are all in place early, so the Hunsford, Pemberley and elopement turns fire under pressure without stopping for explanation. The middle stretch (S23–S31) is slower and more reportorial, and several file labels misname their content, which can make the timeline harder to trace.

firstFinding.headline: The parents' temperaments are fixed from the first chapter, and the plot runs on them
bullets: Mrs. Bennet's single aim (marrying off her daughters) drives the Collins pressure in S20, the Brighton push in S41 and her euphoria in S49.
Mr. Bennet's sarcastic detachment sets up his permissiveness in S41 and his late self-reproach in S48.
firstFinding.subject: Parental temperament as causal engine

supportingRefs.quote: When the first transports of rage which had produced his activity in seeking her were over, he naturally returned to all his former indolence.

firstFinding.evidenceQuote: The business of her life was to get her daughters married: its solace was visiting and news.
